correctness.rationale: The ten-vertex Kneser graph and full S5 automorphism group are proved from its five four-vertex independent stars. All proper colourings are in bijection with independent-set partitions and injective palette assignments. A least-vertex exact-cover recursion proves enumeration completeness. A second restricted-growth recursion, independently generated four-palette named-colour assignments, the ordinary chromatic polynomial identity and full automorphism cycle census reproduce all counts. No finite-to-infinite extrapolation is used: the polynomial identity holds for all integer q>=0 by the colour-class bijection and direct algebra.

originality.rationale: Collins–Trenk (2006) proves only the previously known minimum proper distinguishing palette size four for the Petersen graph. The inspected generalized Petersen work (Weigand–Jacobson 2008; Lal–Bhattacharjya 2009) studies thresholds and constructions, rather than this full named-palette count and complete class-stabilizer census. Arvind–Cheng–Devanur (2008) supplies general distinguishing-labeling enumeration methods without the proper-colouring requirement or a Petersen polynomial. The new exact degree-ten polynomial, full stabilizer counts, two precise four-block types and 10/q^3 failure law are not given by the checked texts or earlier available claims. Unindexed historical equivalence is a residual risk.
residual_risks: Historical combinatorics tables may contain the same polynomial under an alternate name such as proper distinguishing colour partition enumerator.
A prior automorphism-orbit classification could in principle permit the four-colour subcount, although not the newly computed full variable-palette polynomial.
No independent external scientific audit was performed.

value.rationale: The exact probability of proper colour assignments that genuinely break graph symmetry is a natural quantitative refinement of the classical distinguishing chromatic number. For the maximally symmetric canonical Petersen graph, the full degree-ten polynomial, the complete stabilizer-order spectrum, two geometric four-block types and the ten-transposition high-palette failure coefficient give structural information not available from the existence threshold. The exact finite invariant is a reusable baseline for testing symmetry-breaking colouring methods; no inflated general graph-family implication is claimed.
